needs_human.note: A shared sidecar becomes two independent files after a rename or move, so a later edit to one does not reach the other.; A sibling row marked missing claims sidecars just as a trashed one does, so renaming the surviving video leaves a copy for a file that may never return. No test covers the missing state.; Purging a trashed sibling removes only its own file (fileops.py:719-741), so the original the trashed row was claiming stays with no owner.; With a same-stem sibling, renaming `movie.mp4` to `movie.ja.mp4` copies `movie.ja.srt` and then finds the bare target occupied, because the claimed original was not moved away. The new video's bare track is then the old language track. This is reasoned from subtitle.py:141-149 and no test covers it.; A partial `shutil.copy2` failure can leave a truncated target, which detect_subtitles offers and later runs skip because the target exists.

A claim lasts as long as the row exists, so a missing or trashed sibling that never returns makes each later rename copy instead of move. Purging that row (physical_delete at fileops.py:719) does not remove the sidecar it claimed, so the original then has no owner.; Two copies of a shared sidecar diverge once either is edited. No document says a shared subtitle stops being shared after one video leaves.; A sidecar arriving under a new stem becomes a track of any existing video with that stem, or of `x.mp4` when it arrives as `x.ja.srt`. For example, renaming `other.mp4` to `movie.ja.mp4` beside `movie.mp4` gives `movie.mp4` a Japanese track holding other's bare subtitle. r1 reported the general form and it is unchanged.; `shutil.copy2` to a shared target can leave a partial file on failure, and detection would offer it while the next attempt would skip it because the target exists. This is the same shape as the partial `shutil.move` copy r1 noted, now also reachable on the same drive.
